name: Rotated Klee-Minty Problem
description:
The development, assessment, and comparison of randomized search algorithms
heavily rely on benchmarking. Regarding the domain of constrained optimization,
the number of currently available benchmark environments bears no relation to
the number of distinct problem features. The present paper advances a proposal
of a scalable linear constrained optimization problem that is suitable for
benchmarking Evolutionary Algorithms. By comparing two recent EA variants, the
linear benchmarking environment is demonstrated.
general_score_metric: best objective value (often reported alongside number of function evaluations or success rate)
reputation: A well-known synthetic test problem in the evolutionary computation and numerical optimization communities used to stress solver behavior on linear constrained problems.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; synthetic and scalable linear constrained problem. Small/controlled problem family that can lead to overfitting of algorithmic components; performance typically reported as objective value and runtime/FE budget rather than a single accuracy metric.
